Daily Brief

The day's news is dominated by President Trump's pledge to pay every American adult $5,000 if Republicans win November's midterm elections—a proposal costing over $1.3 trillion that Democrats have dismissed as an 'empty promise' and legal experts question [BBC, France 24, Le Monde]. Trump also stated that the ongoing US-Iran war will not end until after the elections, linking oil prices to the conflict's resolution [BBC]. In Germany, Chancellor Merz clashed sharply with AfD leader Weidel in parliament following the far-right party's historic 44% victory in Saxony-Anhalt, with Merz condemning AfD's migration policies as amounting to 'ethnic cleansing' [BBC]. Russia's deployment of new jet-powered drones against Ukraine has intensified dramatically, with attacks rising from 350 in June to 2,800 in August, outpacing Ukrainian air defenses [BBC]. Meanwhile, a ferry fire in the Philippines has left at least five dead and 86 missing near the tourist destination of Coron [BBC, Le Monde, Nikkei Asia]. On the climate front, the EU's Copernicus monitor confirmed August 2026 as the hottest month ever recorded globally [RFI].

01 Policy

Trump Pledges $5,000 to Every American Adult if Republicans Win Midterms

  • President Trump announced at the first-ever midterm Republican convention in Texas that every American adult would receive $5,000 if the GOP wins both chambers of Congress in November
  • The plan would cost approximately $1.3 trillion for nearly 270 million American adults; Trump provided no details on funding or implementation, though VP Vance linked it to tariff revenues
  • Democrats dismissed the pledge as an 'empty promise' and legal experts questioned whether a president has authority to issue such payments
  • Trump argued short-term economic pain from the Iran war is worth preventing Tehran from developing nuclear weapons

03 Geopolitics

Germany's Merz Clashes with AfD After Far-Right Party Wins 44% in Saxony-Anhalt

  • The Alternative for Germany (AfD) won nearly 44% of the vote in Saxony-Anhalt, falling three seats short of an outright majority—no far-right party has held power in a German state since WWII
  • Chancellor Friedrich Merz attacked AfD in parliament, calling it a 'destructive force' with migration policies amounting to 'ethnic cleansing' for skilled workers
  • AfD leader Alice Weidel responded that voters had shown Merz's coalition with the center-left was a 'total failure'
  • US President Trump praised the result, linking it to 'horrible immigration rules and regulations'; the AfD has been labeled 'right-wing extremist' by German domestic intelligence

04 Conflict

Russia's Jet-Powered Drones Overwhelm Ukraine's Air Defenses with Daily Attacks

  • Russia fired new jet-powered Geran drones against Ukraine every day throughout August, marking the first month of daily attacks with the upgraded weapons
  • Ukrainian military reported jet-powered drone attacks rose from 350 in June to 1,600 in July and 2,800 in August
  • The drones can cruise at over 300 mph, significantly faster than older models and beyond the speed of Ukrainian interceptors
  • Some turbojet engines powering the drones are reportedly sourced from China, according to Ukrainian military intelligence

05 Society

Philippines Ferry Fire Leaves Five Dead and 86 Missing Near Palawan

  • The MV June Aster caught fire near Coron, Palawan, while carrying 117 passengers and 17 crew members from Manila
  • At least five people have died and 86 remain missing; 43 survivors have been rescued
  • Survivors reported hearing a loud explosion from the cargo hold before fire rapidly spread; some passengers were not wearing life vests
  • Rescue efforts were hampered by darkness, strong waves, and thick smoke; the cause remains under investigation
